function.description: Retrieve specific details about museums, such as opening hours and ticket prices. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

The user says "國家博物館" which could refer to Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History or National Museum of American History. But maybe they mean "National Museum" generically. Details: "Opening hours", "Adult tickets", "Child tickets". The function expects details: "Opening hours" | "Adult tickets" | "Child tickets"[].

So we call function twice: one for Washington DC, one for Paris. But we need to specify which museum? The function only takes location, not museum name. It might return info for all museums in that location? That seems ambiguous. But we can pass location: "Washington DC" and details: ["Opening hours", "Adult tickets", "Child tickets"]. Similarly for "Paris".

But the function signature: details: "Opening hours" | "Adult tickets" | "Child tickets"[]. That means details can be a single string or an array? It's ambiguous. But likely it's an array of strings. We'll pass array.

Thus we call function twice.
